data.title: How AI referrals are impacting traffic at 4 online retailers
data.description:
In early 2026, leading online retailers that had spoken with Digital Commerce 360 about traffic from artificial intelligence platforms shared a consistent metric: less than 2% of their website referrals had come from AI.

Now, in the final months of 2026, trends among leading retailers indicate that AI site traffic is generally accounting for about 5% of referrals.

In July alone, Digital Commerce 360 previously reported, AI-associated referral traffic to ecommerce sites rising by 62% year over year. In addition, shoppers referred by AI tools generated 53% more revenue per visit than other shoppers.

And findings based on AI Commerce Rankings data from Digital Commerce 360 and ReFiBuy offer a glimpse into which large language models (LLMs) account for the largest shares of AI traffic to online retailers from the Top 1000 Database. That market research tool ranks online retailers in North America by annual web sales.

Four online retailers — including one in the Top 1000 — have shared what trends they’ve noticed so far regarding AI traffic referrals, as of early September.

Impact of AI traffic referrals on retailers in late 2026

1. Bero

The percentage of traffic arriving to non-alcoholic beer brand Bero’s website through AI referrals is “definitely less than five,” according to Hyojin Park, senior director of ecommerce solutions and growth.

“I also think any session reporting, it’s not — at least it’s not yet — advanced to tell you exactly what’s coming from where in terms of AI,” Park said.

Instead, session reporting defaults to identifying what could be AI traffic.

“Whenever I go deep into the referral sources and different referral URLs and paths, once in a while I do see a ChatGPT or something like that, but it’s nothing significant,” Park shared.

She said that in Bero’s case, AI-referral traffic is “not really growing quickly,” which surprised her. The last times she checked, she said, it wasn’t exponential growth “like everything else AI.”

“But still, I know that it’s something that could change,” Park said. “Every three months, something is changing.”

2. Povison

“Traffic from AI platforms is becoming a meaningful new growth area, and it has expanded faster than we initially expected,” according to online furniture retailer Povison’s founder and CEO, Ayden Lin.

The retailer began this year to incorporate AI search and generative discovery into its broader ecommerce strategy, he explained.

He shared that AI-referred traffic currently accounts for about 5% of Povison’s total website traffic. It also continues to grow steadily. Based on the current trajectory, he said Povison expects its share of AI-referral traffic to reach about 10% by early 2027.

“These users tend to be highly informed and move through the decision process relatively quickly,” Lin said. “They actively look for detailed product information and compare options within a shorter period of time. They are especially interested in the combination of value and practical utility, and they have higher expectations for accurate recommendations and fast, responsive service.”

Ahead of the holidays, Povison is working to improve how frequently AI assistants recommend the retailer’s furniture.

3. La Joya Jewelry

Nishit Mehta, founder of La Joya Jewelry, said his retailer saw about 2% to 3% of referral traffic coming from AI sources at the beginning of the year. Since then, it has increased to about 5% or 6%.

“But what I found is that that traffic is very focused, and it converts much better than normal organic traffic or paid traffic,” Mehta told Digital Commerce 360. “I guess the thinking behind it is you’ve been told that this is a good company, so you’re more likely to believe it, and that’s why conversions are better.”

He added that conversion rates for users arriving from large language models (LLMs) are double-digits higher than those who are not arriving through AI referrals. As an example, he said, if La Joya Jewelry’s conversion rate is normally 3%, it rises to more than 13% for users arriving through AI channels.

However, they are not necessarily spending more. He said he hasn’t any trends indicating that users arriving from AI referrals spend more with the retailer than than their counterparts. Rather, the biggest trend is that they’ve done already their research.

La Joya Jewelry, which sells lab-grown diamonds, had to explain in 2024 and 2025 what made them different from natural diamonds. That has been a negligible part of the retailer’s traffic in 2026, according to Mehta.

“In jewelry, everyone has their own budget as to what they want to spend,” Mehta said. “They have it in their minds, so it’s never going to be — very rarely going to be — you want to buy three pieces of jewelry at the same time , unless it’s cheap jewelry, like 150, 200 bucks.”

4. Edible Brands

Erica Randerson, chief digital officer at Edible Brands, said the AI traffic “is still a small percentage of the pie.”

Less than 10% of Edible Brands’ website traffic comes from AI referrals, she told Digital Commerce 360. And of that chunk, ChatGPT accounts for about 95% of all AI-referral traffic to Edible Brands, she shared.

She added that AI traffic “seems to be a little more immune to” consumers seeking lower-priced goods. The average order value (AOV) from that traffic is $5.50 greater than the retailer’s site average.

The conversion rate from AI traffic referrals to Edible Brands’ website is strong, too, she said, at more than 5%.

“But I will say: That’s lower than our site average,” Randerson noted.

She explained that Edible’s conversion rate on its website is more than 10%. It benefits from being a gift-centered retailer.

“We have a high intent audience,” Randerson said. “They’re coming in knowing who they’re shopping for most of the time.”

Edible Brands is No. 182 in the Top 1000 Database. The market research tool tracks North America’s largest online retailers, ranking them by annual ecommerce sales and more.

Edible Brands is also No. 581 in Digital Commerce 360’s new AI Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

data.title: Watsco expands plumbing footprint with acquisition of The Granite Group
data.description:
Watsco Inc. will acquire plumbing and heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) distributor The Granite Group.

The deal, announced on Sept. 14, adds 82 locations to Watsco’s network and deepens its push into plumbing distribution. Terms were not disclosed, and the deal is expected to close following standard regulatory approvals. 

Watsco is the largest HVAC distributor in North America with $7.24 billion in annual revenue in 2025. 

What The Granite Group brings to Watsco

The Granite Group, which reported nearly $500 million in annual sales, serves 11,000 customers from its locations across New Hampshire, Vermont, Maine, Massachusetts, Connecticut, Rhode Island and New York. 

It carries about 29,000 SKUs sourced from more than 450 vendors and has achieved a 10% compounded annual growth rate in sales since 2010.

“The Granite Group is one of the most respected, entrepreneurial businesses in our industry,” said Albert Nahmad, chairman and CEO at Watsco, in a released statement.

Nahmad praised The Granite Group’s “ownership culture” and expressed confidence that it would continue to grow with Watsco.

The Granite Group will continue to operate independently, led by its existing management team, including CEO Bill Condron.

“Watsco was the logical choice for The Granite Group in that we remain independent while gaining access to Watsco’s scale, capital, and the most advanced technology platforms in the industry,” Condron said in a written statement.

Watsco’s growth strategy

Acquiring The Granite Group was part of Watsco’s “Buy and Build” growth strategy, the company said. Since 1989, Watsco has acquired 73 businesses in the HVAC and plumbing industries by identifying successful distributors, supporting their leadership teams, and using its suite of customer-facing technology to grow those businesses, according to Watsco.

On June 1, Watsco closed on its acquisition of  Jackson Supply Company, an HVAC distributor with $230 million in annual sales serving Sunbelt states, including Louisiana, Texas, Mississippi and Oklahoma. In June, Jackson Supply had already contributed about $20 million to Watsco’s revenue, with plans to eventually double the business.

Watsco is actively seeking further investment opportunities in the HVAC and plumbing sectors, it added.

Watsco ecommerce continues to grow

In the first half of 2026, Watsco’s ecommerce sales grew 13%, outpacing overall sales growth of 1%. Online sales accounted for $2.7 billion, or 37% of total revenue in the twelve months ended June 30.

Over the past five years, Watsco has invested more than $250 million into its digital platforms, with plans to continue investing about $68 million annually. Those investments include customer engagement tools, AI capabilities, and internal platforms, Watsco said.

The company expects ecommerce to continue growing through the end of the year, noting that it also has better margins than other sales for the distributor.

data.title: Holidays, made-to-order process drive Polywood sales
data.description:
When Ben Spiegel joined Polywood in 2025, he didn’t anticipate 75% of the outdoor furniture retailer’s sales would come from ecommerce.

He joined the retailer as chief information officer in April 2025 before becoming chief digital officer about a year later. Prior to that, he worked at Health & Beauty and consumer-packaged goods merchants, where sales are largely online. But his expectations for Housewares & Home Furnishings were different.

“I didn’t really expect coming into the category that people would do that,” Spiegel told Digital Commerce 360. “I realized quickly that that’s driven by: you can’t get good products locally — the ones that you want —meaning you go in a showroom and you see something, but it’s not the right color, not the right size, not the right availability. So I’ve been really impressed by our D2C demand and the demand to transact online in this category.”

He identified what he considered to be a problem in the category: Mass Merchants and Home Improvement retailers sell a few outdoor furniture products each. Additionally, consumers ordering from “some obscure vendor” wouldn’t know when a product will arrive or what brand it is.

In addition to selling direct-to-consumer (DTC), Polywood sells wholesale and through showrooms.

Polywood’s made-to-order delivery process

“The interesting part about our businesses is it’s vertically integrated, just-in-time manufacturing, meaning you literally click on checkout on Shopify and it triggers lumber being moved to a machine, being extruded, being cut and being shipped to you,” Spiegel said. “So [it’s] this whole idea of one-piece flow versus manufacturing massive amounts of inventory and then trying to push it.”

Upon ordering, Polywood products generally ship out in about five to seven business days, according to Spiegel. He estimated that the retailer keeps a maximum of 5% of its inventory on hand.

“We make each piece custom,” Spiegel said. “That means we can give a massive assortment without having to worry about carrying too much inventory, which is a really different approach.”

Polywood’s peak sales periods

As a brand for outdoor products, the vast majority of Polywood’s business — around 80% — occurs between Memorial Day and Labor Day. May alone is a key month for the retailer.

It largely limits itself to sales around those two holidays, but it participates in other promotional periods in different ways. For example, during the Cyber 5, Polywood tends to avoid discounting. However, it might offer faster shipping or limited-time products.

Polywood also sells via Amazon and experienced an increase in traffic during the marketplace’s Prime Day event in June this year.

“It was a noticeable spike, and the main issue with this spike is that it was a lot of add to carts and comparison shopping,” Spiegel explained. “Our average purchase price is about $1,600, so we are not as much in the realm of the spontaneous, ‘Hey, I’m emotionally triggered to buy this right now,’ and a lot more in this space of ad planning the purchase.”

In fact, Polywood’s approach to Prime Day is to reduce ad spend. Such promotional periods are when Polywood might sell chairs at the retailer’s lowest price points, he added. That compares to selling dining or deep-seating sets during its busier periods.

“If you’re searching for a dining set and you see Polywood at full price and everybody else at a discount price, it doesn’t really make sense,” Spiegel said.

Polywood also offers sales centered around the 4th of July. This year’s didn’t go as well as 2025, though, he said.

“We see the higher-income level, higher-priced product is not impacted as much,” Spiegel said. “We see the lower-household income/household smaller purchases were dramatically less just due to the soft consumer environment and people’s uncertainty.”

How Polywood prepares for the Cyber 5

Spiegel noted the value of “second-season states” for Polywood during the Cyber 5. He told Digital Commerce 360 that he lives in Florida.

“I don’t go outside until it’s November,” Spiegel said. “So as you think about Black Friday, as you think about that whole season, that is our ‘second season’ with all the southern states. That’s when they do these things, and that’s when we really double down again.”

He explained that the outdoor furniture product space “is always a push sale.” It doesn’t benefit as much from coupon shopping. Rather, Spiegel said, if a consumer is going to buy, then it’s just a matter of when.

To account for that, Polywood focuses on developing the right reach, frequency and context relevance in its ecommerce operations. That involves working with social media influencers and creators to get the retailer into roundups. He gave an example of a roundup called “top five outdoor chairs for your winter yards.” Polywood has more success with that than with the pay-to-click space during the Cyber 5, he said.

Spiegel also noted that purchases windows are about twice as long during the Cyber 5 as compared to its usual sales. Normally, he said, Polywood customers will convert in their first seven days of coming to a retailer’s site. During the Cyber 5 in 2025, he said, that period extended to about 10 to 14 days.

Customers began searching earlier for deals to fill their baskets, he said. Polywood also has two white-label brands, which Spiegel said helps the retailer to see when its customers fill other baskets as well. Once they fill their baskets, he said, they’re waiting to see who will make them an offer first.

“Is there going to be a flash sale? So it becomes this kind of stalking, hunting period for a lot of consumers, which was good for Google and Facebook because we spent more because we have to keep driving them to the site,” Spiegel said. “But it was a lot of just put in your cart and wait, which required us to change our conversion optimization windows and adjust our email and ping and retargeting campaigns to match that.”

He compared the period to tax-refund season, when consumers add to their carts “and they start dream shopping. And then, when it becomes time, they all check out at once.”

data.title: Ecommerce Trends: How marketing budgets are adapting to AI-driven purchases
data.description:
Artificial intelligence (AI) platforms are wielding increasing influence on where and how customers shop online — and as they do, retailers appear to be changing how they spend on marketing and ads.

The findings come from new research published by Northwestern University’s Retail Analytics Council and the AI-powered shopping assistant maker Minty. In their findings, published Sept. 16, analysts assessed that cashback apps, deal platforms and price-comparison tools have become the “most helpful” channels for shoppers when compared with traditional advertising, loyalty programs, retail media and creator marketing.

The responses in the report reflected perspectives from 150 senior commerce decision-makers at retailers, brand manufacturers and online marketplaces, according to Minty. Among those participants, 98% of those providing answers came from companies whose annual revenue exceeded $100 million.

Those companies agreed to share where they intended to spend their marketing budgets as they look ahead.

What are online retailers’ marketing priorities as shoppers turn to AI?

In the survey results, 79% of respondents indicated that they expect their primary customer base to be using AI tools in 2027. Moreover, 81% of participants checked cashback and savings tools as the most helpful form of marketing they saw shoppers using to make purchase decisions.et78

“This isn’t marketers tweaking a line item,” said Frank Dudley, associate director of the Retail Analytics Council at Northwestern University. “They’re responding to a fundamental shift in how products are discovered and chosen.”

Digital Commerce 360 and Bizrate Insights’ own survey results in 2026 found that finding better deals was the No. 1 reason that shoppers used AI tools.

Dudley sees marketing budgets following shopping behavior as AI technology adoption proceeds.

“As consumers increasingly rely on AI to compare prices, evaluate alternatives, and maximize value, brands are reallocating investment toward the channels and capabilities that influence those decisions,” he stated.

What AI adoption means for marketing spending

Also in the new survey results, two-thirds of marketers said they believed AI would be the primary way they would reach shoppers in 2027. More than half of those marketers are using AI in tandem with their savings offerings as a result.

In addition, half of the marketers surveyed noted that they were marketing directly to AI agents. The same answer sets showed that only 18% anticipated that traditional search would be their primary means of reaching shoppers in 2027. 13% said the same for social media channels.

Minty refers to marketing toward online shoppers at early stages of their journeys when they are using AI agents as “proactive commerce.”

“Buying decisions are moving earlier in the ecommerce purchase funnel,” noted Rodney Mason, chief marketing officer at Minty. “Proactive commerce, delivering total-value-messaging to shoppers and their AI agents before they search, click or abandon a cart, is already being practiced by the largest market leaders and the majority of respondents intend to do so in 2027.”

Importantly, the shift is already affecting budgets among many surveyed in the study. Among marketers who target shoppers in these early research stages on AI platforms, 61% said they have either increased marketing spending or reallocated existing budgets toward cashback and savings apps.

data.title: Costco brings Uber Eats delivery to new US locations
data.description:
Costco is taking its Uber Eats delivery partnership nationwide, expanding from 17 states to nearly 600 warehouse locations across all 47 states where the retailer operates.

Instacart remains a major delivery partner and continues to power several of Costco’s delivery experiences. But now the warehouse retailer is continuing to broaden its delivery network for last-mile and same-day service.

In Costco’s fiscal Q2 2026 earnings call in March, chief financial officer Gary Millerchip noted that same-day delivery through Instacart, Uber Eats and DoorDash was growing faster than overall Costco digital sales, which themselves were up 22.6% year over year. 

Costco is No. 7 in the Top 2000 Database. The database is Digital Commerce 360’s ranking of the largest online retailers in North America by their annual ecommerce sales. It’s also the fourth-largest Mass Merchant in the database.

Details of Costco’s Uber Eats expansion

Through the expanded partnership, Costco’s full warehouse inventory is available for delivery through Uber Eats. Members enter their Costco membership number in the Uber Eats app to shop, then choose between on-demand and scheduled delivery.

The two companies are also adding cross-promotional benefits designed to deepen the relationship between their respective membership programs. Costco members can receive 50% off an annual Uber One membership during their first year, followed by 20% off in subsequent years. Uber One benefits include no delivery fee, savings on rides and delivery orders, and member-only promotions. 

Uber and Uber Eats gift cards are also available at Costco locations and on Costco.com for a discount, and consumers can purchase a Costco membership directly through Uber Eats and save 30% on their first order.

“We are thrilled to expand our partnership with Costco nationwide, giving Costco members more ways to shop and bringing the brand’s storied selection and value to more consumers,” said Andrew Macdonald, President and Chief Operating Officer at Uber.

 “Costco is one of the largest and most trusted retailers in the country for good reason, and our nationwide partnership demonstrates the scale and opportunity Uber can bring to retailers looking to meet more of consumers’ everyday shopping needs,” Macdonald added.

What is Costco’s multi-partner delivery strategy?

Same-day delivery has become a point of pride for Costco. 

“Same-day delivery powered by our third-party partners has become a highly effective way to deliver more convenience to our members,” Costco CEO Ron Vachris told investors during a May earnings call. 

He added that average same-day delivery time in the US is now 45 minutes, with an average customer satisfaction rating of 4.8 out of 5.

“This part of our business is growing at an even faster rate than our digital business overall,” Vachris continued. “And is a strong driver of loyalty, as it is often our highest spending members who are using the service.”

Meanwhile, Instacart remains an integrated partner for Costco. Instacart’s Storefront Pro commerce platform and fulfillment solutions power Costco’s same-day delivery websites in France and Spain, where it launched in January.

Costco members in France and Spain can shop directly through Costco’s websites, rather than through the Instacart app. 

Internationally, Uber Eats already has a significant partnership with Costco. Hundreds of Costco locations are available on Uber Eats across Canada, France, Japan, Spain, Taiwan and Mexico.
